prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1258; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss for the left-turn collision. Insured reports the other vehicle struck the rear quarter panel while the insured was completing a left turn at an intersection. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles received and saved to file.

Entry 2: Spoke with the insured by phone to confirm the sequence of events. Insured states the oncoming vehicle was approaching at speed and did not yield the right of way. Insured denies any distraction and says the turn signal was active. Recorded statement scheduled.

Entry 3: Received notice that the claimant is represented by counsel. All further contact with the claimant to go through the attorney of record. Letter of representation placed in file. Claimant's medical records requested under signed authorization from counsel.

Entry 4: Claimant's counsel submitted a demand package citing neck and back strain following the collision. Records show initial treatment at an urgent care facility, followed by physical therapy referral. Treating provider notes reduced range of motion in the cervical and lumbar regions. Reviewing for consistency with the reported mechanism of impact and prior treatment history.

Entry 5: Liability assessment in progress. Based on the police report and statements, the left-turning insured appears to bear primary responsibility, though comparative fault is still under review. Referred the bodily injury evaluation to the claims supervisor and set a follow-up to request an independent medical examination through counsel.
